svg.title: ACH netting and settlement — high-level architecture
svg.desc: Vertical data flow from participant banks through S3 drop zone, ingestion service, Kafka topic, netting engine, and settlement service to Federal Reserve, with supporting services Redis cache, RTN registry, netting state DB, and settlement store on the right, and a rejection path on the left.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('In the ACH netting POC, how do participant banks submit NACHA files?')
sendPrompt('How does the S3 file drop zone work in our ACH netting architecture?')
sendPrompt('Walk me through every step the ingestion service performs on a NACHA file')
sendPrompt('Why does validated transaction data go through Kafka before the netting engine?')
sendPrompt('How does the netting engine accumulate bilateral positions per RTN pair?')
sendPrompt('How does the settlement service compute and publish final net obligations?')
sendPrompt('How does TCH interact with the Federal Reserve to achieve final irrevocable settlement?')
sendPrompt('What happens to a NACHA file that fails ingestion validation — how is the bank notified?')
sendPrompt('What exactly is cached in Redis during ingestion and what is the eviction strategy?')
sendPrompt('What data is in the RTN participant registry and how does ingestion use it?')
sendPrompt('How is netting state persisted and recovered across a settlement cycle?')
sendPrompt('What records does the settlement store hold and who reads them after settlement?')
